Course: IT 202 - Computer Programming 1
Program: BSIT
Description: This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

CLO1. Define and analyze the
computing requirements needed for
an effective solution that is essential
for developing holistic and impactful
solutions.
[EGA 1,3,4] [PO 1,2,3,6,8]

This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

[EGA 1,3,4] [PO 1,2,3,6,8]

This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

fieldValue.t:
This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

cases.targetText:
This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

Course: IE-402 - Systems Engineering
Program: BSIE
Description: This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

cases.sourceText:
Course: IE-402 - Systems Engineering
Program: BSIE
Description: This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

[EGA 2] [PO 4,5]

This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

cases.targetText:
This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

fieldValue.t:
This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

Case Study Discussion:
Systems Engineering
as a Human Activity
Provide a case study that
highlights the role of
human factors in systems
engineering, including
team dynamics,
stakeholder involvement,
and ethical
considerations. Facilitate
a class discussion on the
human-centered aspects
and their impact on
project outcomes.
Design and Conduct
Experiments Activity
Assign students a mini-
project to design and
conduct an experiment to
validate a system
component or process.
They should identify the
objective, develop a
methodology, collect
data, and analyze results
to inform design
improvements.
Robust Design
Brainstorming Session
(Robust Design I)
In small groups, students
brainstorm how to apply
basic robust design
principles to make a
system more stable
under varying conditions.
They discuss factors that
influence system stability
and propose design
adjustments to minimize
variability.
Advanced Robust
Design Project (Robust
Design II)
Activity: For a more
complex project, students
apply advanced robust
design techniques to a
hypothetical or real-world
system. They identify and
control multiple variables
to minimize performance
variation across diverse
scenarios.

Definitions of the values named (from the institution's published wording; approval status: pending_approval):
- Courage: Courage is the strength to stand firm in truth and goodness. It is the freedom to express one’s thoughts responsibly, the boldness to give and receive fraternal correction, and the integrity to choose what is right even when it is difficult or unpopular. Rooted in Gospel values, courage empowers us to live authentically and faithfully in service of God and others.
- Humility: Humility allows us to see ourselves and others through the lens of truth and grace. It teaches us to acknowledge both our strengths and limitations, to welcome correction with openness, and to use every experience as an opportunity for growth. Above all, humility reminds us to be grateful to God who created each of us uniquely for a purpose greater than ourselves.

Course title: Systems Engineering
Course code: IE-402
Program: BSIE
cases.targetText:
This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

advanced techniques

system.

ilos.text: ILO11: Analyze and evaluate multiple design alternatives through trade space exploration, applying criteria to select the optimal concept based on performance, feasibility, and stakeholder needs. [CLO 3] [CLO4]

ILO 12: Develop and execute experiments to validate design assumptions, analyze system behaviors, and refine solutions, demonstrating an understanding of experimental design and data collection principles. [CLO 3] [CLO4]

ILO 13: Identify critical factors in system design that influence performance consistency, and apply robust design techniques to improve reliability under varying conditions (Robust Design I). [CLO 3] [CLO4]
ILO14: Utilize advanced robust design methods to enhance system resilience, focusing on minimizing performance variability in complex, multi-variable systems (Robust Design II). [CLO 3] [CLO4]

fieldValue.activities:
Case Study Discussion:
Systems Engineering
as a Human Activity
Provide a case study that
highlights the role of
human factors in systems
engineering, including
team dynamics,
stakeholder involvement,
and ethical
considerations. Facilitate
a class discussion on the
human-centered aspects
and their impact on
project outcomes.
Design and Conduct
Experiments Activity
Assign students a mini-
project to design and
conduct an experiment to
validate a system
component or process.
They should identify the
objective, develop a
methodology, collect
data, and analyze results
to inform design
improvements.
Robust Design
Brainstorming Session
(Robust Design I)
In small groups, students
brainstorm how to apply
basic robust design
principles to make a
system more stable
under varying conditions.
They discuss factors that
influence system stability
and propose design
adjustments to minimize
variability.
Advanced Robust
Design Project (Robust
Design II)
Activity: For a more
complex project, students
apply advanced robust
design techniques to a
hypothetical or real-world
system. They identify and
control multiple variables
to minimize performance
variation across diverse
scenarios.
fieldValue.tasks:
Robust Design I –
System Evaluation
and Improvement
Proposal
Task: Have students
apply basic robust
design techniques to
evaluate a system
and propose design
changes that would
make it more stable
under varying
conditions. They
should identify critical
factors that affect
performance and
suggest
improvements to
minimize variability.
Robust Design II –
Advanced Design
Analysis
Task: For a more
complex system,
students should apply
advanced robust
design methods to
assess and improve
the system’s
performance. They
will use tools such as
design of experiments
(DOE) to explore
multiple design
variables and their
interactions.
Robust Design
Report (I & II)
Task: Students will
submit a report for
each part of the
robust design
application, detailing
the steps taken to
assess and improve
system performance.
For Robust Design I,
they will focus on
basic principles, and
for Robust Design II,
they will apply
advanced techniques
to optimize the
system.

Case Study Discussion:
Systems Engineering
as a Human Activity
Provide a case study that
highlights the role of
human factors in systems
engineering, including
team dynamics,
stakeholder involvement,
and ethical
considerations. Facilitate
a class discussion on the
human-centered aspects
and their impact on
project outcomes.
Design and Conduct
Experiments Activity
Assign students a mini-
project to design and
conduct an experiment to
validate a system
component or process.
They should identify the
objective, develop a
methodology, collect
data, and analyze results
to inform design
improvements.
Robust Design
Brainstorming Session
(Robust Design I)
In small groups, students
brainstorm how to apply
basic robust design
principles to make a
system more stable
under varying conditions.
They discuss factors that
influence system stability
and propose design
adjustments to minimize
variability.
Advanced Robust
Design Project (Robust
Design II)
Activity: For a more
complex project, students
apply advanced robust
design techniques to a
hypothetical or real-world
system. They identify and
control multiple variables
to minimize performance
variation across diverse
scenarios.

Robust Design I –
System Evaluation
and Improvement
Proposal
Task: Have students
apply basic robust
design techniques to
evaluate a system
and propose design
changes that would
make it more stable
under varying
conditions. They
should identify critical
factors that affect
performance and
suggest
improvements to
minimize variability.
Robust Design II –
Advanced Design
Analysis
Task: For a more
complex system,
students should apply
advanced robust
design methods to
assess and improve
the system’s
performance. They
will use tools such as
design of experiments
(DOE) to explore
multiple design
variables and their
interactions.
Robust Design
Report (I & II)
Task: Students will
submit a report for
each part of the
robust design
application, detailing
the steps taken to
assess and improve
system performance.
For Robust Design I,
they will focus on
basic principles, and
for Robust Design II,
they will apply
advanced techniques
to optimize the
system.

Course: CpE 304 - Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors
Program: BSCPE
Description: This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

rawSourceEvidence.raw:
This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

fieldValue.t:
This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

Course title: Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors
Course code: CpE 304
Program: BSCPE
cases.targetText:
This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

cases.sourceText:
Course title: Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors
Course code: CpE 304
Program: BSCPE
Course objectives (CLOs):
CLO 1: Identify the design process of electronic circuits and systems and conduct experiments involving sensors and mixed-signal systems, analyze data, and interpret results to improve performance and reliability.
CLO 2: Develop analytical and design skills for both analog and digital electronic circuit and implement sensor-based systems that integrate hardware and software components while considering economic, environmental, and ethical constraints.
CLO 3: Analyze and apply the behavior of passive components in AC circuits and their instrumentation applications in multidisciplinary teams to design, test, and optimize mixed-signal and sensor applications for engineering solutions
CLO 4: Exhibit lifelong learning, precision, and ethical responsibility in performing measurements and calibration tasks. Engage in continuous learning by exploring emerging technologies and trends in sensors, instrumentation, and mixed-signal design for future innovation

fieldValue.title: CLO 1
fieldValue.statement: Identify the design process of electronic circuits and systems and conduct experiments involving sensors and mixed-signal systems, analyze data, and interpret results to improve performance and reliability.

fieldValue.title: CLO 2
fieldValue.statement: Develop analytical and design skills for both analog and digital electronic circuit and implement sensor-based systems that integrate hardware and software components while considering economic, environmental, and ethical constraints.

fieldValue.title: CLO 3
fieldValue.statement: Analyze and apply the behavior of passive components in AC circuits and their instrumentation applications in multidisciplinary teams to design, test, and optimize mixed-signal and sensor applications for engineering solutions

fieldValue.title: CLO 4
fieldValue.statement: Exhibit lifelong learning, precision, and ethical responsibility in performing measurements and calibration tasks. Engage in continuous learning by exploring emerging technologies and trends in sensors, instrumentation, and mixed-signal design for future innovation

Course title: SYSTEM INTEGRATION AND ARCHITECTURE 1
Course code: IT-202
Program: BSIT-CYBERSECURITY

outcomes.vision: Moved by the Spirit of the Risen Christ, La Consolacion University Philippines, envisions itself to become a catalyst for the wholistic transformational development of Catholic Augustinian Marian graduates rooted in Gospel values.

mission.lead: To achieve the above vision, LCUP commits itself to generate and make available to its Augustinian Marian students, programs and services that will make them:
items: exhibit academic and technical competence in their respective areas of discipline in the local and international environment;
demonstrate their knowledge, critical thinking and creativity by exploring the various avenues of learning and searching for truth;
manifest their willingness to serve specially the marginalized sector of our society;
demonstrate productivity in various areas of learning as responsible citizens of the society; and
live the Gospel values in the varied aspects of their personal and professional lives

pos.text: Articulate and discuss the latest developments in the specific field of practice;
Effectively communicate orally and in writing using both English and Filipino;
Work effectively and independently in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural teams;
Act in recognition of professional, social ethical responsibility;
Preserve and promote “Filipino historical and cultural heritage;
Analyze complex problems, and identify and define the computing requirements needed to design and appropriate solution;
Apply computing and other knowledge domains to address real-world problems;
Design and develop computing solutions using a system-level perspective;
Utilize modern computing tools.

description.t:
This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

clos.title: CLO 1
clos.statement: Define and analyze the computing requirements needed for an effective solution that is essential for developing holistic and impactful solutions.

clos.title: CLO 2
clos.statement:  Incorporate ethical standards and social responsibility into technical designs, ensuring that solutions serve the common good, in line with Marian and Augustinian principles of truth and compassion. 

clos.title: CLO 3
clos.statement: Collaborate effectively within multi-disciplinary and culturally diverse teams to develop Java- based programming solutions that address social challenges, demonstrating social responsibility and cultural sensitivity.

clos.title: CLO 4
clos.statement: Demonstrate the Filipino- Catholic Augustinian Spirituality through value webbing.

institution.vision: Moved by the Spirit of the Risen Christ, La Consolacion University Philippines, rooted in Gospel values as a Catholic Augustinian-Marian institution, envisions to become a catalyst for the holistic transformation of all persons and communities.

mission.lead: LCUP commits to generate and make available to all persons and communities’ programs and services that will enable them to:
items: exhibit academic and technical competence in their respective areas of discipline in the local and international environment;
demonstrate their knowledge, critical thinking and creativity by exploring the various avenues of learning and searching for truth;
manifest their willingness to serve specially the marginalized sector of our society;
demonstrate productivity in various areas of learning as responsible citizens of the society; and
live the Gospel values in the varied aspects of their personal and professional lives.

pos.text: Apply computing and other knowledge domains to address realworld problems.
Analyze complex problems and identify and define the computing requirements needed to design an appropriate solution.
Design and develop computing solutions using a system-level perspective.
Demonstrate ethical behavior as an IT Professional and sensitivity to the impact of technology in the society.
Show Augustinian virtues/ethical values and the understanding and appreciation of corporate social responsibility.
Work effectively and independently in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural teams.
Understand the impact of their work on society and strive to ensure that their actions contribute positively on the community.
Articulate and discuss the latest developments in the specific field of practice.
Act in recognition of professional, social and ethical.

Demonstrate ethical leadership and social responsibility by integrating sustainability, inclusivity, mental well-being and peace-building principles into academic, professional and community engagements, ensuring holistic development and societal transformation.

description.raw:
This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

outcomes.vision: Moved by the Spirit of the Risen Christ, La Consolacion University Philippines, envisions itself to become a catalyst for the wholistic transformational development of Catholic Augustinian Marian graduates rooted in Gospel values.

mission.lead: To achieve the above vision, LCUP commits itself to generate and make available to its Augustinian Marian students, programs and services that will make them:
items: exhibit academic and technical competence in their respective areas of discipline in the local and international environment;
demonstrate their knowledge, critical thinking and creativity by exploring the various avenues of learning and searching for truth;
manifest their willingness to serve specially the marginalized sector of our society;
demonstrate productivity in various areas of learning as responsible citizens of the society; and
live the Gospel values in the varied aspects of their personal and professional lives

description.t:
This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

complex project, students
apply advanced robust
design techniques to a
hypothetical or real-world
system. They identify and
control multiple variables
to minimize performance
variation across diverse
scenarios.

description.raw:
This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

outcomes.vision: Moved by the Spirit of the Risen Christ, La Consolacion University Philippines, envisions itself to become a catalyst for the wholistic transformational development of Catholic Augustinian Marian graduates rooted in Gospel values.

mission.lead: To achieve the above vision, LCUP commits itself to generate and make available to its Augustinian Marian students, programs and services that will make them:
items: exhibit academic and technical competence in their respective areas of discipline in the local and international environment;
demonstrate their knowledge, critical thinking and creativity by exploring the various avenues of learning and searching for truth;
live the Gospel values in the varied aspects of their personal and professional lives;
manifest their willingness to serve specially the marginalized sector of our society;
demonstrate productivity in various areas of learning as responsible citizens of the society; and
develop individuals who are resilient, inclusive and responsive to be socio-economic realities of the Philippines and the complexities of the global environment.

description.t:
This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

clos.title: CLO 1
clos.statement: Identify the design process of electronic circuits and systems and conduct experiments involving sensors and mixed-signal systems, analyze data, and interpret results to improve performance and reliability.

clos.title: CLO 2
clos.statement: Develop analytical and design skills for both analog and digital electronic circuit and implement sensor-based systems that integrate hardware and software components while considering economic, environmental, and ethical constraints.

clos.title: CLO 3
clos.statement: Analyze and apply the behavior of passive components in AC circuits and their instrumentation applications in multidisciplinary teams to design, test, and optimize mixed-signal and sensor applications for engineering solutions

clos.title: CLO 4
clos.statement: Exhibit lifelong learning, precision, and ethical responsibility in performing measurements and calibration tasks. Engage in continuous learning by exploring emerging technologies and trends in sensors, instrumentation, and mixed-signal design for future innovation

title.raw: Fundamentals of Mixed Signals and Sensors

description.raw:
This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.

items: exhibit academic and technical competence in their respective areas of discipline in the local and international environment;
demonstrate their knowledge, critical thinking and creativity by exploring the various avenues of learning and searching for truth;
manifest their willingness to serve specially the marginalized sector of our society;
demonstrate productivity in various areas of learning as responsible citizens of the society; and
live the Gospel values in the varied aspects of their personal and professional lives.

outcomes.vision: Moved by the Spirit of the Risen Christ, La Consolacion University Philippines, rooted in Gospel values as a Catholic Augustinian-Marian institution, envisions to become a catalyst for the holistic transformation of all persons and communities.

mission.lead: LCUP commits to generate and make available to all persons and communities’ programs and services that will enable them to:
items: exhibit academic and technical competence in their respective areas of discipline in the local and international environment;
demonstrate their knowledge, critical thinking and creativity by exploring the various avenues of learning and searching for truth;
manifest their willingness to serve specially the marginalized sector of our society;
demonstrate productivity in various areas of learning as responsible citizens of the society; and
live the Gospel values in the varied aspects of their personal and professional lives.

pos.text: Articulate and discuss the latest developments in the specific field of practice;
Effectively communicate orally and in writing using both English and Filipino;
Work effectively and independently in multi-disciplinary and multi-cultural teams;
Act in recognition of professional, social ethical responsibility;
Preserve and promote “Filipino historical and cultural heritage;
Analyze complex problems, and identify and define the computing requirements needed to design and appropriate solution;

outcomes.vision: Moved by the Spirit of the Risen Christ, La Consolacion University Philippines, rooted in Gospel values as a Catholic Augustinian-Marian institution, envisions to become a catalyst for the holistic transformation of all persons and communities.

mission.lead: LCUP commits to generate and make available to all persons and communities’ programs and services that will enable them to:
items: exhibit academic and technical competence in their respective areas of discipline in the local and international environment;
demonstrate their knowledge, critical thinking and creativity by exploring the various avenues of learning and searching for truth;
manifest their willingness to serve specially the marginalized sector of our society;
demonstrate productivity in various areas of learning as responsible citizens of the society; and
live the Gospel values in the varied aspects of their personal and professional lives.

outcomes.vision: Moved by the Spirit of the Risen Christ, La Consolacion University Philippines, rooted in Gospel values as a Catholic Augustinian-Marian institution, envisions to become a catalyst for the holistic transformation of all persons and communities.

mission.lead: LCUP commits to generate and make available to all persons and communities’ programs and services that will enable them to:
items: exhibit academic and technical competence in their respective areas of discipline in the local and international environment;
demonstrate their knowledge, critical thinking and creativity by exploring the various avenues of learning and searching for truth;
manifest their willingness to serve specially the marginalized sector of our society;
demonstrate productivity in various areas of learning as responsible citizens of the society; and
live the Gospel values in the varied aspects of their personal and professional lives.

live the Gospel values in the varied aspects of their personal and professional lives.

outcomes.vision: Moved by the Spirit of the Risen Christ, La Consolacion University Philippines, rooted in Gospel values as a Catholic Augustinian-Marian institution, envisions to become a catalyst for the holistic transformation of all persons and communities.

mission.lead: LCUP commits to generate and make available to all persons and communities’ programs and services that will enable them to:
items: exhibit academic and technical competence in their respective areas of discipline in the local and international environment;
demonstrate their knowledge, critical thinking and creativity by exploring the various avenues of learning and searching for truth;
manifest their willingness to serve specially the marginalized sector of our society;
demonstrate productivity in various areas of learning as responsible citizens of the society; and
live the Gospel values in the varied aspects of their personal and professional lives.
